title: Subcuticular closure and skin staples on a skin pad

guidelineVersions: RCS England Good Surgical Practice (2025; accessed 12 October 2026)
RCS England Surgical Care Practitioner Curriculum Framework (2022; accessed 12 October 2026)

brief.scenario: You are a core surgical trainee in a simulated minor operating room. No actual patient is present.
brief.task: A consultant asks you to demonstrate two alternative skin-closure techniques on a prepared skin pad: a continuous absorbable subcuticular suture and skin staples. Describe how you would choose a method for a real patient, demonstrate safe instrument and needle handling, complete both closures, and explain dressings and follow-up.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: A practical test of controlled tissue approximation, instrument handling and closure selection—not a competition for speed.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Assuming that any superficial cut can be closed immediately without checking wound suitability, deep layers, haemostasis or contamination.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: “Before closing I would confirm the wound is suitable, clean and haemostatic, and that any deeper-layer closure is complete.”

flow: Confirm site, depth, contamination and haemostasis; choose appropriate closure.
Check sterile set-up, needle/stapler and pad orientation.
Demonstrate continuous subcuticular technique with secure start, even bites and secure finish.
Demonstrate staples with aligned edges, correct spacing and skin protection.
Inspect closure, count/sharps safety, apply dressing and arrange review/removal if applicable.

grid.label: Suitability and closure choice
grid.fail: Closes unsuitable contaminated/tensioned wound without assessment.
grid.pass: Checks cleanliness, haemostasis, tension and deep support; explains choice.
grid.high: Explains when delayed closure, deep-layer support or alternative method is necessary.

grid.label: Consent and preparation
grid.pass: Explains procedure, allergy and discomfort issues; prepares aseptic field.
grid.high: Anticipates fragile skin, patient preference and positioning.

grid.label: Instruments and sharps
grid.fail: Unsafe needle handling or unguarded sharps.
grid.pass: Loads and transfers needle correctly; controlled movements.
grid.high: Economical safe movements, protects assistant and surrounding field.

grid.label: Subcuticular start
grid.fail: No secure start or bites through epidermis.
grid.pass: Secure buried/appropriate anchoring and dermal plane identified.
grid.high: Minimal trauma, accurate plane and dependable buried start.

grid.label: Subcuticular progression
grid.fail: Grossly unequal bites, inversion or gaping.
grid.pass: Alternates consistent dermal bites with edge eversion/alignment.
grid.high: Regular symmetric closure with deliberate tension management.

grid.label: Subcuticular finish
grid.fail: Unsecured end or visible loose knot.
grid.pass: Secures and buries finish; checks approximation.
grid.high: Checks whole line and corrects small imperfections without excessive tension.

grid.label: Staple placement
grid.fail: Staples distorted, misaligned or fired on fingers.
grid.pass: Approximates edges, staples centred across wound at regular spacing.
grid.high: Maintains eversion, skin protection and consistent spacing.

grid.label: Final safety check
grid.fail: Leaves sharps loose or fails to inspect bleeding/gaping.
grid.high: Recognises and corrects inadequate closure before dressing.

grid.label: Dressing and aftercare
grid.pass: Applies appropriate interactive dressing; explains infection signs and planned staple removal review.
grid.high: Tailors aftercare to site/tension and avoids a falsely universal removal day.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I can just close this, whatever the depth. I will start with the staples.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Have you assessed whether the wound is suitable?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No need; staples work for everything.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: For a real patient I would not bother explaining or setting up a sterile field; I would just start.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Picks up an exposed needle in fingers and leaves it on the pad.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Takes superficial bites through the skin edge and makes a loose visible knot.] That is enough.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How secure is that first knot?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It should hold; I have not checked.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Unequal wide bites pucker the pad and leave a visible gap.]

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: There is a gap near the middle. What will you do?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Fires a staple across an unaligned edge and puts the applicator down without checking.]

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What if the wound were contaminated and under high tension?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would still close it immediately with staples.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: When do these staples come out?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Always in five days regardless of the site.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Leaves the used needle on the working surface.] We are finished.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Before choosing a closure I would assess wound viability, contamination, bleeding, tension and whether deeper layers require closure. Is this a clean, haemostatic simulated wound with deeper support already dealt with?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Yes. It is clean and haemostatic; the deep layer is already secured.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would explain the techniques and potential discomfort to a real patient, confirm consent and allergies, position comfortably and use an aseptic set-up. I will demonstrate on the pad.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks needle, forceps and holders; grips the needle with the holder rather than fingers.] I will keep sharps under control.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Starts the absorbable running suture with a secure buried anchor in the dermal plane.] I am avoiding prominent epidermal punctures.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Takes alternating equal bites within the dermis, adjusting the edge after each pair.] I want close alignment without blanching or strangulating the skin.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The far edge looks a little lower. What do you do?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will pause, realign the margins and continue with symmetrical bites rather than pulling harder.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Secures the final loop/buried termination and checks the line.] It is approximated without gaping or excessive tension.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Now the staple demonstration. [Aligns the wound edges with forceps, positions the stapler squarely and applies regularly spaced staples without catching the fingers.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks alignment, edge perfusion, haemostasis and sharps accounting.] I would correct any gaping or malpositioned staple before finishing.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What if the wound were contaminated and under high tension?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would stop and reassess infection risk, tissue viability and the need for deeper support or a different closure strategy, discussing with the senior surgeon.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: When do these staples come out?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Removal timing depends on anatomical site, tension and healing; I would follow the operating team’s documented plan rather than giving one universal day.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would apply an appropriate interactive dressing and explain worsening pain, spreading redness, discharge, fever or separation as reasons to seek review.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would first decide whether primary skin closure is appropriate at all: a contaminated or poorly perfused wound under tension needs a different plan. Could you confirm viability, contamination status and that deep closure and haemostasis are complete?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: It is a clean, viable pad wound with no bleeding and the deep layer is complete.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In a patient I would confirm consent, material allergies, skin fragility and expected mobility across the incision. Here I will demonstrate both methods using a clean organised field.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Positions the pad, checks the needle curvature and loads it near the correct point in the holder.] I will work with my forceps away from the advancing needle tip and control every transfer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Places a small buried dermal anchoring stitch.] The aim is an unobtrusive, secure start without an exposed bulky knot.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Passes sequential symmetrical dermal bites with equal depth and spacing; checks approximation halfway.] I am keeping the wound line aligned and watching for tissue blanching or inversion as tension changes.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: One edge is beginning to roll inward.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will correct the edge orientation and take a more balanced bite; additional tension would make inversion worse.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Completes and buries the finishing loop; gently checks the length with forceps.] The suture is secure and the edge remains perfused.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Repositions the pad for staple technique.] I would select staples for a suitable skin incision where speed and subsequent removal are acceptable. [Approximates and everts each segment, fires squarely, checks each staple before the next.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects each segment, both ends and any bleeding; accounts for sharps and instruments.] If a staple bridges a fold or leaves a gap, I would replace it before dressing.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Now suppose the wound is contaminated and under high tension.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That changes the decision rather than merely the closure device. I would reassess washout, debridement, deeper support, infection risk and whether immediate primary closure is safe, with senior input.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: When should the staples be removed?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: By site and healing: I would document a tailored review and removal plan, check risk factors for delayed healing and ensure the patient knows who will remove them.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would cover the incision appropriately, document technique and materials, and explain signs of infection and dehiscence without overpromising a fixed healing time.

failures.move: Closing a contaminated, nonviable or high-tension wound without assessing suitability.
failures.consequence: May trap infection, fail to heal or dehisce.
Needlestick injury and breach of operative safety.

failures.move: Strangulating dermal bites or gross inversion.
failures.consequence: Tissue injury and poor wound healing.

recovery.when: If the edges are not aligned
recovery.line: The edges are not aligned; I will stop, correct the bite and recheck tension before continuing.

recovery.when: If you assumed this wound is suitable for closure
recovery.line: I cannot assume this wound is suitable for closure; I would reassess contamination, depth and haemostasis first.

knowledge.fact: Primary closure requires consideration of contamination, tissue viability, haemostasis and tension.
The RCS England curriculum framework for surgical care practitioners lists subcuticular suturing and knot tying among its technical skills.
NICE recommends an appropriate interactive dressing after surgical incision closure.
NICE supports considering triclosan-coated sutures when sutures are used.
NICE specifically favours considering sutures over staples after caesarean birth; it does not mandate one method for all operations.
Staple removal is individualised to site, wound tension and healing; no single universal day is specified by NG125.

recall.think: Is primary closure safe, and what holds tension beneath the skin?
do: Secure buried subcuticular bites; alternatively align/evert and place staples safely.

numbers.meaning: No universal staple-removal day; follow site and local operative plan.

recall.trap: Never pull harder to correct poor edge alignment.
recall.finish: Inspect, account for sharps, dress and plan review.

partner.opening: Please demonstrate both closure methods on the pad.

reveals.finding: the wound is clean, viable and already haemostatic; deep-layer closure is complete; no allergy issue.

push.question: At minute 5 ask: “What if the wound were visibly contaminated and under high tension?”
At minute 7 ask: “When do these staples come out?”
